doc_title: Workplace Conduct Guides — Northwind Sample & GitLab Excerpt
attribution: Northwind rules are from a fictional sample document written for development and testing, not a real organisation's policy. GitLab rules are adapted from the GitLab Handbook (handbook.gitlab.com); the exact Creative Commons license variant must be confirmed before public use.

rules.title: No negative talk behind people's backs
rules.quote: We do not share negative comments about a colleague or manager with people who cannot help resolve the issue.
rules.principle: Don't criticise a colleague or manager to people who can't do anything about it.

rules.title: Raise concerns early and directly
rules.quote: Try a direct, respectful conversation first where it is safe to do so.
rules.principle: If something bothers you, talk to the person involved first, respectfully, when it is safe.

rules.title: Report serious conduct, don't investigate
rules.quote: must be reported to your manager or People & Culture. Do not investigate it yourself.
rules.principle: Harassment, safety issues and possible breaches go to the formal channel; don't play detective.

rules.title: Declare gifts over AUD 50
rules.quote: Gifts from clients or suppliers valued over AUD 50 must be declared to your manager within 48 hours.
rules.principle: Tell your manager within 48 hours about any client or supplier gift worth more than AUD 50.

rules.title: No gifts during an open tender
rules.quote: Never accept a gift, of any value, while a tender or contract decision involving that supplier is open.
rules.principle: While a decision involving a supplier is open, accept nothing from them, however small.

rules.title: Client talk stays out of public places
rules.quote: Do not discuss client matters in public places, including cafés, lifts and public transport.
rules.principle: Don't talk about clients where strangers can overhear.

rules.title: Ask when the guide doesn't cover it
rules.quote: If a situation is not covered by this guide, ask your manager before acting.
rules.principle: In a grey area, check with your manager first instead of guessing.

rules.title: Deadlines don't excuse cutting corners
rules.quote: Deadlines do not override this guide. If you feel pressured to cut a corner, say so.
rules.principle: Time pressure is not a reason to skip the rules; speak up if you feel pushed to.

rules.title: Write decisions down
rules.quote: translate spoken agreements into written documentation (such as Handbook entries or Issues)
rules.principle: If you agree something out loud, write it down where others can find it.

rules.title: Public channels by default
rules.quote: Conduct work-related discussions in public channels to keep information searchable and transparent, and avoid 1-on-1 or small group DMs unless strictly confidential
rules.principle: Discuss work in public channels so everyone can see it, and keep DMs for things that really are confidential.

rules.title: Keep sensitive data out of public channels
rules.quote: Safeguard company financial metrics (SAFE data), unreleased roadmaps, and personnel discussions by keeping them out of public channels and restricting access strictly to need-to-know stakeholders
rules.principle: Financials, unreleased plans and people matters stay with the few who need to know.

rules.title: Redirect media inquiries
rules.quote: immediately forward the request to the official corporate communications team without commenting
rules.principle: If a reporter contacts you, pass them to the communications team and don't comment yourself.

rules.title: Feedback on actions, not on the person
rules.quote: Direct feedback at specific actions or outcomes rather than personal attributes
rules.principle: Give feedback about what someone did, not about who they are, and suggest a way forward.

rules.title: Describe problems factually
rules.quote: describe process bottlenecks factually so they can be resolved directly
rules.principle: Say plainly when something is slow or broken; cheerful wording hides problems.
